newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY ENDS FLAT IN MODERATE TRADE, T/N RATES UP.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY ENDS FLAT IN MODERATE TRADE, T/N RATES UP.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed flat against the basket of currencies on Wednesday after tracking dollar/mark swings for the most of the day in moderate trade, dealers said.
They said traders closed positions before the central bank's fixing after adjusting to the dollar/mark's dip in European trade and a some intraday currency-selling based on small client orders.
"The zloty generally followed dollar/mark swings with some slight intraday currency selling from small client orders," said Piotr Nowak from Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA.

The zloty closed at 2.88/2.84 percent from the trading band centre against yesterday's close at 2.89/2.82 percent. It was at 2.8515/25 to the dollar, up from 2.8595/10 on Tuesday and at 1.8475/85 to the mark, down from 1.8392/10.

The central bank set the maximum 1-day reverse repo rate at 21.30 percent against the last 14-day rate of 19.16 percent, which dealers said was meant to show where the NBP wanted to see one-day rates.
The NBP drained only 21 million zlotys from the system after banks bid for 113 million zlotys against a 300 million zloty offer in the first one-day operation since August 26.
Overnight deposit rates fell one-point despite the drainage as the market's liquidity boosted by Wednesday's 839 million zloty net inflow coming mainly from net T-bill buy-back.

Overnight rates closed at 21.30/22.50 percent, down from opening's 22.50/23.50 percent, but tomorrow/next rates were at 22.10/24.10 percent, up from 21.15/22.85 at 1015 GMT signalling banks expected the market to tighten again on Thursday.

The November money supply figures showing a 1.4 percent rise against 2.2 percent in October were in line with this year's plan making the overall 1996 broad money growth target plausible, analysts said. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
